title: CetiRun AI Gateway Helm Chart Values Schema
description: JSON Schema for validating CetiRun AI Gateway chart values

global.description: Values propagated by the cetirun-platform umbrella chart

registry.description: Registry host override for the Gateway image

replicaCount.description: Number of Gateway replicas. Above 1 requires Redis: the bundled Valkey or redis.host.

operatorIntegration.description: Serve CetiRun Agents: derive shared-model deployment/access-group bindings from chart configuration, reserve the copilot/ model-name prefix for per-Agent GitHub Copilot routes, and check router fallback targets against the caller's key (general_settings.enforce_fallback_model_access). The cetirun-platform chart turns it on.

image.description: Gateway container image: open-source LiteLLM on Azure Linux, built from app/cetirun-ai-gateway

repository.description: Image repository. global.registry, when set, replaces the registry host.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty uses global.version, then the chart appVersion.

digest.description: Image digest. When set, the reference is pinned to exactly this image.

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for private registries

nameOverride.description: String to override the default name

fullnameOverride.description: String to override the default fullname

models.description: Models exposed by this Gateway, in LiteLLM model_list format. The list can be empty. With operatorIntegration, AgentPolicy shared-model bindings require chart-configured models; model_info.id and cetirun-model- access groups are chart-owned. Names beginning with cetirun- are reserved, and so are names beginning with copilot/ while operatorIntegration is on.

litellm_params.description: Parameters passed to LiteLLM, including the provider-prefixed model and a credential reference

blockUnpricedModels.description: Refuse requests to models whose price LiteLLM does not know. A model missing from the price table costs zero, and budget checks are skipped for zero-cost models, so a budget would silently not apply. Azure OpenAI deployment names are not in that table.

router.description: How a request reaches one of the deployments that serve its model_name, and what happens when that deployment fails. Rendered into LiteLLM's router_settings and general_settings.

failover.description: Send a request that failed on one deployment once more, to another deployment of the same model_name (LiteLLM's enable_weighted_failover). Not a retry of the failed deployment.

continuationAffinity.description: Send a Responses API request that continues an earlier response (previous_response_id) to the deployment that produced it.

encryptedContentAffinity.description: Keep each Responses API conversation on the deployment that encrypted its reasoning, or one with the same endpoint and key (LiteLLM's encrypted_content_affinity). For a model_name served by more than one Azure OpenAI resource or OpenAI organization.

fallbacks.description: Models to try when a request to a model fails: a list of maps from a model_name to the model_names to try, in order.

contextWindowFallbacks.description: Models to try when a request is too long for the model's context window, in the format of fallbacks.

healthChecks.description: Background probes of the deployments of the configured models, and routing only to those that answered. Models added through the console or registered by the CetiRun operator are never probed.

enabled.description: Run the probes and route by their results

providerCredentials.description: Provider API keys, surfaced as environment variables and referenced from models as os.environ/NAME

existingSecret.description: Name of an administrator-owned Secret holding provider keys

auth.description: Gateway platform credentials, distinct from provider keys and agent virtual keys

masterKey.description: Admin API key for the LiteLLM management API

saltKey.description: Encrypts provider credentials stored in the database. Must never change: there is no rotation path, and losing it makes stored models unreadable.

postgresql.description: PostgreSQL holds virtual keys, spend records and models added through the console. Bundled by default, or your own through urlSecret.

bundled.description: Single-instance PostgreSQL deployed with the Gateway, on a persistent volume

urlSecret.description: Secret holding the connection URL of your own PostgreSQL, used when bundled.enabled is false

redis.description: Coordinates budget and rate-limit state between replicas. Required above one replica. Bundled Valkey by default, or your own through host.

bundled.description: Single-instance Valkey deployed with the Gateway, password protected, no persistence

passwordSecret.description: Secret holding the Redis password: your own server's, or the bundled Valkey's in place of a generated one. Required for the bundled Valkey when the chart is rendered with helm template.

requestLog.description: One JSON line of metadata on stdout for every model call, for the cluster's container log collection. No request or response content. Registered by the image's entrypoint, not in LiteLLM's configuration.

enabled.description: Write the line for each call

spendLogs.description: LiteLLM's own row per call in LiteLLM_SpendLogs, read by the console's request log pages. Spend, budgets and daily usage totals are kept either way. Turned off only together with the request log. The cetirun-platform chart turns it off.

enabled.description: Write a row to LiteLLM_SpendLogs for each call. false needs requestLog.enabled.

metrics.description: LiteLLM's Prometheus metrics, served on a separate port without authentication

port.description: Port of the metrics endpoint, at /metrics. Unset, it is 9090, or 9091 when service.port is 9090. Must differ from service.port.

excludeLabels.description: Labels left out of every metric

podMonitor.description: A PodMonitor for the Gateway pods, created only when the cluster serves its API

apiVersion.description: azmonitoring.coreos.com/v1 for Azure Monitor managed Prometheus, monitoring.coreos.com/v1 for the Prometheus Operator

migrations.description: Apply database migrations from an init container in each Gateway pod; pods take turns

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: How long a stopping replica may spend finishing requests it has already accepted

dependencyImage.description: Image of a bundled dependency, pinned by tag and optional digest
